finalists.label: Acute Pericarditis
finalists.why: The ECG findings of ST-segment elevations with PR-segment depression in leads II, III, and aVF, and the patient's symptoms of constant chest pressure radiating to the right jaw, diaphoresis, and vomiting, strongly support this diagnosis.

finalists.label: Acute Coronary Syndrome
finalists.why: The elevated serum troponin I level and ECG findings of ST-segment elevations with PR-segment depression in leads II, III, and aVF, are indicative of this condition, despite the normal coronary arteries.

frontier_selector.why: The specific ECG findings and the patient's symptoms, such as chest pressure radiating to the jaw and diaphoresis, are more characteristic of Acute Pericarditis, and the normal echocardiogram results do not rule out this diagnosis.
